template.name: Smallest Strength
template.storyMechanic: Everyone (including the hero) expects the solution to require a big, obvious action; instead, the actual solution requires a quiet quality the hero already has (patience, listening, kindness), which is revealed to be powerful precisely because it was underestimated.
sceneStructure: Big expectation: hero (or others) assumes the problem needs a big, loud, obvious action.
Big attempt fails: hero (or another character) tries the big action and it does not work.
Quiet quality noticed: hero notices a small, quiet quality in themselves that seemed unrelated to solving anything.
Quiet action: hero uses that quiet quality directly on the problem.
Resolution: the quiet action succeeds where the big attempt could not, and the true belief reframes strength itself.
template.repetitionNote: T09 is a single-inversion template â€” it works through contrast (big vs. small), not repeated structure. Do not add a three-part repetition here.
template.escalationPattern: Escalation is expectation-based: the story keeps implying the quiet quality is irrelevant, right up until it becomes the entire solution.
template.turningPoint: The 'quiet quality noticed' beat â€” the moment the hero (or the story) stops dismissing the small strength and starts trusting it.
template.resolutionPattern: Resolution must explicitly show the quiet quality succeeding where the big/loud attempt failed, so the inversion is legible, not just implied.
template.symbolIntegrationPoint: Symbol is closely tied to the quiet quality itself â€” introduced alongside it, so the symbol and the strength are recognized together.
illustrationOpportunities: A small, quiet moment where the hero's real strength is visible
Resolution showing the quiet strength working, framed gently rather than dramatically
template.pageRhythmGuidance: Give the big attempt bold, busy page composition, then shift to quiet, spacious, minimal composition for the quiet action and resolution â€” the page design itself should embody the inversion.

events.label: BIG_EXPECTATION
events.action: Arin is wearing a shirt that feels scratchy and irritating. Arin wanted to get comfortable. The uncomfortable clothing keeps distracting Arin. Everyone around Arin, and Arin too, believed "I can't be okay when things feel uncomfortable." — so the fix had to be something big and obvious — snapping back louder, arguing harder, pushing through the annoyance by sheer stubbornness — because surely a problem this loud needed a big enough reaction to match it.

events.label: BIG_ATTEMPT_FAILS
events.action: So Arin tried exactly that — raising a voice, tugging and huffing and complaining at full volume — but it did nothing to fix the real trouble: the uncomfortable clothing keeps distracting Arin, still there, unchanged, no matter how big the reaction got.

events.label: QUIET_QUALITY_NOTICED
events.action: Then, in the middle of all that noise, Arin noticed something small and quiet instead — the irritation grows until ordinary things start feeling unbearable, and underneath it was a tired, uncomfortable body asking to be listened to.

events.label: QUIET_ACTION
events.action: So Arin stopped pushing and did the quiet thing instead — paused, took a slow breath, and gave the body what it had been asking for all along, so Arin could finally get comfortable, without any fuss or fighting at all.

events.label: RESOLUTION
events.action: That is what worked — not the loud reaction, which had changed nothing, but the quiet act of caring for the body underneath it, and Arin understood: I can stay peaceful even when my surroundings aren't perfect.
